story: Students join the AI Creators Guild, a studio that takes on real creative missions. Each module is a Quest Line that ends with a Boss Challenge (the final project). Students earn XP for learning behaviours (not just talent), level up from Prompt Rookie to AI Architect, collect badges, and compete in four Houses whose scores are averaged so team size doesn't matter. The same system runs all year so students always know how to progress.

xpRules.notes: Effort counts — any honest attempt earns it.
Each lesson's build has 1–2 checkpoints shown on the board.
Every member of the winning team; 5 XP to all teams that finish.
Specific feedback using the 'I like / I wonder / Try' frame.
Catching a real hallucination or bias and proving it with a source.
Rubric score 1–4 per criterion × 25 XP; up to 100 per criterion bands.
Optional advanced add-on to the final project.

levels.name: Prompt Rookie
levels.perk: Guild nickname + avatar (made with AI in Launch).

levels.name: Story Weaver
levels.perk: Pick your build partner for a lesson.

levels.name: Web Smith
levels.perk: Your work featured on the class showcase wall.

levels.name: Flow Builder
levels.perk: Become a Guild Mentor (earn peer-teaching XP).

levels.name: App Engineer
levels.perk: Propose a side quest for the class.

levels.name: Game Designer
levels.perk: Skip one exit ticket (still do the build!).

levels.name: AI Architect
levels.perk: Certificate + name on the Guild Hall of Fame.

badges.name: Safety Pact
badges.how: Signed the AI Safety Pact and passed the safety quiz.

badges.name: Prompt Duelist
badges.how: Completed the Launch Boss: Prompt Duel.

badges.name: Pixel Forger
badges.how: Shipped a complete Brand Kit (Images Boss).

badges.name: Hook Master
badges.how: Shipped a disclosed AI video (Video Boss).

badges.name: Web Smith
badges.how: Published a landing page + store (Web Boss).

badges.name: Fact Checker
badges.how: Caught 3 real AI mistakes and proved them with sources.

badges.name: Ethics Guardian
badges.how: Spoke up about a consent, copyright or honesty issue in a respectful way.

badges.name: Guild Mentor
badges.how: Helped 5 classmates get unstuck (without touching their keyboard).

badges.name: Bug Hunter
badges.how: Found and fixed a bug by explaining it to the AI precisely.

badges.name: Iteration Station
badges.how: Showed 5+ documented versions of one piece of work.

badges.name: On a Roll
badges.how: 10 exit tickets in a row completed.

rituals.name: Recall Raid
rituals.how: 5 quick questions mixing THIS module and older modules; houses answer on mini-whiteboards.
rituals.principle: Spaced retrieval + interleaving: pulling older ideas back out strengthens memory far more than re-reading.

rituals.name: Prompt of the Week
rituals.how: Best student prompt from last week is shown and dissected with the Prompt Recipe.
rituals.principle: Worked examples from peers lower cognitive load and show what 'good' looks like.

rituals.name: Spot the AI Mistake
rituals.how: Teacher shows an AI output with a planted or real error; first house to prove it with a source wins.
rituals.principle: Elaborative interrogation: asking 'is this true and how do I know?' builds critical thinking.

rituals.name: Gallery Walk
rituals.how: Laptops open, students rotate and leave sticky-note feedback: I like / I wonder / Try.
rituals.principle: Peer teaching and feedback: explaining and judging work deepens understanding.

rituals.name: Boss Week
rituals.how: Final project build + showcase with rubric; Boss defeated = module badge.
rituals.principle: Project-based learning: applying many skills together makes knowledge transferable.

moduleHooks.questLine: Join the Guild: make your avatar, learn the rules of AI.
A startup hires the Guild to create its visual identity.
The startup needs a launch video that people actually watch.
Give the brand a home on the internet and a store.
The studio is overwhelmed — build robot helpers.
Build an app for yourself — your own tool.
The Guild's arcade: remix a classic, then invent your own.
Show the world what the Guild built.

fairness: Most XP comes from effort behaviours (attempting, revising, helping) so every student can level up — not only the fastest.
House scores use the AVERAGE XP per member so uneven team sizes stay fair.
Leaderboards show houses publicly; individual XP is shown privately or as top-10 only, to avoid shaming.
Re-shuffle houses never; instead rotate build partners so students work across houses.
Award XP live with the tracker (2 clicks) and keep it fast — the game should never eat lesson time.
